newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 190-195 bcf in wkly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 190-195 bcf in wkly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 190-195 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 150 bcf to 225 bcf for the week ended January 17.
"A lot of people are expecting a big draw. If it comes in well-below 200, it could be bearish," said one Texas-based trader, adding eastern stocks should remain well-above last year's levels.
Another trader agreed. "On a degree day basis, we were colder last week than in any week last year. It was cold everywhere."
In last report, overall stocks fell by 127 bcf, slightly above expectations, and climbed to a 139 bcf surplus to last year. The four week average drawdown is 100 bcf.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 105 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would cut the surplus to last year to about 50 bcf. In 1996, eastern storage fell by 61 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 29 bcf and western stocks by 15 bcf.
While producing and consuming region west inventories continued to lag 1996 levels, stocks in the critical eastern region were 263 bcf, or almost 28 percent, above year-ago.
